extracted.intended_audience: newspaper publishers, editors, press association members, and professional journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for newspapers and press associations on preserving press freedom (internationally and domestically) and on practical wartime newspaper operations — editorial, production, distribution, and organizational measures. Includes advocacy points for press representation at peace conferences and procedural steps to protect independence and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: News free at source / equal transmission facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "News at its source shall be freely available to all everywhere; and ... that no country shall give preferential transmission facilities to its own press as against the press of any other country."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents of individual newspapers and press associations everywhere should have direct and equal access to the news of all governments and equal facilities of transmission to their own countries. This is presented as a concrete guarantee to seek at peace conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press must assume militant leadership for international news freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The American press should assume militant leadership to obtain international news freedom at the next peace conference; the press must drop its passive role and be intensively active.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press should attain unity of purpose, establish leadership and present principles of idealism internationally; seek seats or influence at peace negotiations to demand clauses protecting free press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppression and control of the press as a prime cause of wars
rubrics_metrics.description: The address treats 'suppression and control of the press by governments' as 'a prime cause of wars.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This premise is the rationale for press statesmanship: the press should advocate internationally against suppression because perverted news facilitates war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid monopoly in news-gathering; encourage mutual ownership and competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders 'in no sense sought a monopoly' and were 'opposed to the creation of a monopoly as a menace to national interest'; competition (multiple agencies) is desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure news organizations to prevent monopolistic control; preserve competition and consider mutualization of agencies to reduce risk of owner-political influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent exclusive access to government news / resist subordination to governments
rubrics_metrics.description: "Exclusive access to the news of governments can only be gained by a news service through its subordination to the government...That means that the government's news story can be told in only one way, the government's way, with the resulting perversion of the truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure multiple independent channels to governmental news so no single government-controlled service has exclusive access, which would enable perversion of truth to serve state purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of news at the source fosters honesty and truth
rubrics_metrics.description: "Availability of news at the source, with the resulting competition in getting it and preparing it for publication...will lead to honesty in news...Thus the truth will prevail."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open source access plus competition exposes falsehoods and reduces the effectiveness of 'tainted' news; this principle supports policy demands and operational priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve independence of news agencies (example: Reuters trust)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters was made 'owned by the British press as a whole' and 'its continuance of independence has been legally guaranteed' by a trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use organizational/legal mechanisms (trusts, mutual ownership) to safeguard the independence of national/international news agencies from political or commercial takeover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial priorities in wartime: retain editorial vigor, condense features
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial pages are least cut and leading articles 'kept going as vigorously as ever'; features are condensed; sports and commercial sections have been most severely treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial voice and leading articles even under constraints; condense nonessential features while preserving core editorial content and individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and reporting technique under scarcity: strict brevity and no repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the very biggest stories may exceed 500 words; 'Every fact is given once only' — eliminate repeating the main facts lower in the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt new editing discipline: shorter copy, single presentation of facts, tighter leads, and stricter story editing to conserve space and newsprint while preserving essential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserve newsprint via advertising restrictions and voluntary rationing
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary restrictions on advertising (limits on total ad space over periods), limits on display ad size (generally about four inches), and balancing ad space across weeks were used to conserve paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impose voluntary limits on advertising space and display-ad dimensions; prioritize essential advertising and avoid large goodwill/commercial ads that would waste scarce newsprint or cause ethical concerns (e.g., at sea-loss cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate in production and distribution to save resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Car pools formed; communal distribution; where two papers exist, one motor carries both; central deposit points instead of many wholesalers; merged runs and cooperative pressroom scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate regionally with other papers to pool transport and distribution, merge press runs where possible, reduce duplication and conserve fuel, manpower, and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut waste and plan exact print runs to maximize newsprint efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut out stops/starts to avoid spoiled copies; maintain exact run numbers; prewar net effective use was ~75% of newsprint, wartime figures improved to ~97%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve pressroom discipline, reduce spoilage, and precisely plan runs to maximize the percentage of newsprint that reaches paid circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merge staffs, multi-skill workers and increased use of women
rubrics_metrics.description: Use women wherever possible; inside specialists reduced; staff become handymen; morning and evening staffs sometimes merged into a single twilight staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-train staff, merge functions and shifts, deploy women and multi-skilled workers to cover labor shortages while retaining operational capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect archives and critical records with redundant backups and secure storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: microfilming circulation books and records, storing earliest files and photographic negatives in coal mines, double sets of labels and wrappers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain duplicates, microfilm/backup vital records, and store archives in secure/alternate locations to ensure continuity after raids or disasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce number of editions and unnecessary production complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Many evening papers reduced editions (e.g., from seven down to one or two); cut edition stops/starts and unnecessary extras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit editions per day to conserve resources and streamline production; combine editions where practicable without sacrificing essential timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase cooperation among competing papers to maintain service
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperation (e.g., shared pressroom times, merged classified plates, mutually agreed advertising limits) has preserved circulation and service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitors should cooperate on logistical and production matters during crises to maintain service to the public while conserving limited resources.
